intro: Passing completely takes longer than you think.

widget.instructions: Press Play to run the motion; scrub the time slider to inspect any instant.

stem: A {{L1}} m train at {{v1}} m/s overtakes a {{L2}} m train moving the same way on a parallel track at {{v2}} m/s.
How long does it take, from the front of the faster train reaching the back of the slower one until it has passed completely?

hints.text: Work in the frame of the slower train. How fast does the faster one move there?

overtake-one-length.text: To pass completely, the faster train must gain both lengths: its own and the other train's.

overtake-speeds-added.text: The trains move the same way, so the faster one gains only at the difference of their speeds.

dimension-mismatch.text: Check the unit: the answer is a time.

workedSolution.text: Gain needed: {{L1}} + {{L2}} = {{Lsum}} m, so t = {{Lsum}} ÷ {{rel}} = {{ans}} s.

overtake-one-length.front: Time for one train to pass another completely?

overtake-speeds-added.front: Relative speed of trains moving the same way?

generic.front: Overtaking time for two trains moving the same way?

accessibility.altText: Two lanes with the two trains moving right at different speeds.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Use Play and the time slider; type your answer in the box.
